jei.simulacra.neural_node: Turns rotation into compute. Feed it a shaft; the faster it spins the more Cognition Units it makes. Nodes placed against each other form one Cognition Array.
jei.simulacra.mainframe_controller: Pools every Neural Node it can reach into one budget and hands it out to the machines that ask. One controller per array.
jei.simulacra.data_cable: Carries compute from a Mainframe Controller to a machine that is not next to it. Passive: it stores nothing and costs nothing.
jei.simulacra.simulation_chamber: Trains a Data Matrix, then spends compute printing Predictions of its subject onto Imprint Blanks. No mobs are ever spawned.
jei.simulacra.loot_fabricator: Spends Predictions on their subject's drops. Runs on rotation rather than compute. Left alone it rolls the subject's loot table; pick a drop on its screen and it makes only that, priced by rarity.
jei.simulacra.blank_data_matrix: Hold one in your off hand and defeat a mob to bind it. Kills feed it data until it is trained, after which a Simulation Chamber can keep teaching it without you.
jei.simulacra.prediction: One roll of its subject's loot table, held in abstract. A Loot Fabricator turns it into a real drop.
jei.simulacra.imprint_blank: What a Simulation Chamber prints onto. Finer grades yield more Predictions per job, and only Pristine can hold a boss.
jei.simulacra.corrupted_imprint: A print that failed. Low-grade models botch some of their jobs; crush one to recover part of the material.
jei.simulacra.resonant_catalyst: Occasionally left behind when a boss subject resonates with its substrate. The renewable route back to Pristine Imprint Blanks.
simulacra.ponder.neural_node_single.head: Turning rotation into compute
simulacra.ponder.neural_node_single.text: A Neural Node takes rotational force on its back shaft and turns it into compute
Faster rotation means more compute, and proportionally more stress
A node on its own still produces nothing. It has to be pooled by a Mainframe Controller.
simulacra.ponder.neural_node_array.text_: Nodes conduct, so a rack of touching nodes counts as one array
Every driven node adds its own compute, and larger arrays run more efficiently
Cable this rack to a Mainframe Controller and the whole array becomes one pool
simulacra.ponder.data_matrix.header: Recording a mob with a Data Matrix
simulacra.ponder.data_matrix.text_1: Hold a Blank Data Matrix in your off hand and kill mobs with it
simulacra.ponder.data_matrix.text_2: The first kill binds the matrix to that mob. From then on only that mob adds data.
simulacra.ponder.data_matrix.text_3: Once it has recorded enough kills the matrix is ready to be trained in a Simulation Chamber
simulacra.ponder.mainframe_controller.he: Pooling an array with the Mainframe Controller
simulacra.ponder.mainframe_controller.te: Driven nodes each generate compute, and touching nodes form a single array
The Mainframe Controller claims every node it can reach and pools their output
Wider arrays run more efficiently, so many slow nodes beat one fast node
simulacra.ponder.data_cable.text_1: Cables join separated racks, so one controller can own an array that is not one solid block
simulacra.ponder.data_cable.text_2: They route in any direction, climbing over obstacles to reach a machine
simulacra.ponder.data_cable.text_3: Anything cabled to the controller draws from the same pool of compute
simulacra.ponder.simulation_chamber_trai: Training a model in the Simulation Chamber
Put a bound Data Matrix into the chamber
Fed with compute, the chamber trains the recording into a working model
A trained model can then be run over and over to print that mob's drops
simulacra.ponder.simulation_chamber_jobs: Every job consumes one Imprint Blank, fed in along the back
Each job prints Predictions of the subject onto the blank, not its drops
One Prediction is worth one roll of that mob's loot table. A Loot Fabricator turns them into the drop you pick
simulacra.ponder.loot_fabricator.text_1: The Loot Fabricator turns Predictions into real drops. Unlike the machines upstream it runs on rotation, not compute
simulacra.ponder.loot_fabricator.text_2: Feed it Predictions from a Simulation Chamber. A funnel in, a funnel out
simulacra.ponder.loot_fabricator.text_3: Left alone it rolls the subject's loot table: one Prediction per roll, and you keep whatever comes out
simulacra.ponder.loot_fabricator_choosin: Open the Fabricator to see every drop its subject has, and pick one
Pick one and it makes only that, one stack of Predictions at a time
Rarer drops cost more Predictions, so choosing never beats simply rolling. It only makes the result predictable
